senses.gloss: ch. same, to float, be on top.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 6:6">Targ. II Kings VI, 6</cite> (h. text <he>ויצף</he>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 15:8">Targ. Y. Ex. XV, 8</cite>.—
<cite ref="Sukkah 53a:13">Succ. 53ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ תהומא וכ׳</he> the waters of the deep came on top and threatened to flood the world; <cite ref="Makkot 11a:18">Macc. 11ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 26b:2">Ḥull. 26ᵇ</cite> <he>איידי דמיא … ק׳ מלעיל</he> because water is heavier, it rests below, and the fruit floats on top.
<cite ref="Chullin 111b:3">Ib. 111ᵇ</cite> <he>דמא … דכבדא ק׳</he> the blood of flesh sinks, that of the liver floats.
Erub. 53ᵇ ותִיקְפֵּי עלת וכ׳ Ms. M. (ed. ותתקפו, Rashi ותתקפי, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.), v. עַלַּת; a. e.—2) to coagulate, curdle.
<cite ref="Chullin 93b:7">Ḥull. 93ᵇ</cite> <he>מִיקְפָּא קָפֵי</he> the blood coagulates, opp. <he>דייב</he>.
<cite ref="Chagigah 16b:17">Ḥag. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>אַקְפּוּ ידייכו</he> let your hands float (rest lightly on the head of the sacrifice).
Sabb. 128ᵇ דמַקְפְּיָא נפשה (or דמְקַפְּיָא Pa.) she (the hen) makes herself float (raises her feet and spreads her wings, so that you have to carry her instead of making her walk).
<cite ref="Kiddushin 72a:11">Kidd. 72ᵃ</cite> <he>א׳ פירא דכוורי וכ׳</he> Ar. (ed. <he>בכוורי</he>) a fish pond overflowed on the Sabbath, and they went and caught fish &c.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 12b:7">B. Mets. 12ᵇ</cite> <he>דא׳ אגמא בכוורי</he> (Rashi a. Ar. <he>דאַקְפָּאִי</he>; Ms. R. 2 <he>קְפָאִי</he>; Ms. R. 1 <he>אכפאי</he>, corr. acc.) when a meadow was flooded with fish (the flood carrying fish over the meadow).
<cite ref="Chullin 120a:17">Ḥull. 120ᵃ</cite> <he>כיון דאַקְפֵּיה וכ׳</he> since he took pains to make the blood thick (by boiling), he proved that he had his mind on it.
